ei.subject: 공통영어1 미래엔(김성연)
ei.title: The Power of Friendliness: Soft but Strong

fullPassage:
A successful presentation relies on employing various presentation skills, such as using friendly gestures, making natural eye contact, and speaking with an appropriate volume. But just as important, well-designed slides play a critical role in effectively conveying your message. Here are some useful tips for improving your presentation slides. First, adopt a "less is more" approach by keeping your slides simple. Limit each slide to five lines of text and use phrases instead of full sentences. This allows the audience to focus more on listening than on reading. Next, prioritize readability by carefully selecting attractive font sizes and colors. The best readability is generally achieved with a font size of at least 18 pt, and you should limit slides to three or four colors to avoid distraction. Lastly, enhance your slides with high-quality images that complement the text. By following these simple tips, you can create effective slides that hold your audience’s interest and keep them engaged from start to finish!

The responsive behavior of dogs also caught the attention of an evolutionary anthropologist, Brian Hare. He conducted an experiment to see how dogs would respond to human gestures compared to wolves, who share the same common ancestor. He placed two cups on the ground with food hidden under only one of them. When he pointed to the cup with the food, the dogs found it easily. The wolves, however, struggled and chose cups at random, paying no attention to his gestures. Dr. Hare concluded that the dogs’ ability to read human gestures allowed them to perform better than the wolves. He explained that dogs, unlike wolves, have developed communicative skills with humans and a sense of friendliness. This explanation sounds reasonable according to several evolutionary biologists. They say that from the common ancestors of these two species, those that acted friendly toward humans evolved into dogs, and those that didn’t became wolves. Furthermore, Dr. Hare suggested that the friendly nature of dogs probably provided them with a survival advantage that allowed their population to grow larger than that of wolves.

I’ll give you another example of how friendliness is related to survival. Dr. Hare and his colleagues designed an experiment with chimpanzees and bonobos. Although the two are genetically similar, they are different in nature. To study their cooperative behavior, Dr. Hare’s team set up a device which required two individuals to pull both ends of a rope at the same time in order to access food on a board. When placed with partners that the chimpanzees knew, they were able to work together to get the food. However, when paired with new partners, the chimpanzees usually failed to get the food, and when they occasionally succeeded, they did not share the food with their partner. The bonobos, on the other hand, got along much better than the chimpanzees. They solved the problem regardless of which individual they were paired with, and they were also more willing to share the food. This research shows that bonobos have a cooperative and friendly nature. Experts suggest that their nature has helped their species survive. Without these characteristics, they could have faced extinction.

In our competitive society, many people believe that only the biggest or the strongest can survive and thrive. However, I propose an alternative view: kindness is the key to success. Isn’t that a comforting thought? We can use the power of our natural kindness to communicate and cooperate with different individuals. We can all benefit from this instead of trying to be better than others. I’d like to end this talk with a message. Think of our society as a bouquet. Just as each flower adds to the beauty when it harmonizes with the others, each person can contribute to a more beautiful world when they cooperate. By being kind and working together, we can truly flourish. Thank you for your attention.

questions.passage: The responsive behavior of dogs also caught the attention of an evolutionary anthropologist, Brian Hare. He conducted an experiment __________ how dogs would respond to human gestures compared to wolves, who share the same common ancestor. He placed two cups on the ground with food hidden under only one of them. When he pointed to the cup with the food, the dogs found it easily.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 실험을 한 목적을 나타내는 to부정사 to see가 적절하다. "~을 알아보기 위해 실험을 수행했다"
det.analysis:
✅ ③ to see: 목적을 나타내는 to부정사 → "알아보기 위해"
❌ ① see: 동사원형 단독 사용 불가
❌ ② saw: 과거형 → conducted와 이중 동사
❌ ④ seeing: 분사 → 목적 표현에 부적절
det.tip: conduct/perform an experiment + to부정사: ~하기 위해 실험하다

questions.passage: He placed two cups on the ground with food hidden under only one of them. When he pointed to the cup with the food, the dogs found it easily. The wolves, however, struggled and chose cups at random, __________ no attention to his gestures. Dr. Hare concluded that the dogs’ ability to read human gestures allowed them to perform better than the wolves.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 주절(struggled and chose)과 동시에 일어나는 부대상황을 나타내는 분사구문 paying이 적절하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ paying: 동시동작 분사구문(현재분사)
❌ ① paid: 과거형 → 접속사 없이 두 절 연결 불가
❌ ② pay: 원형 → 문법적으로 불가
❌ ④ to pay: to부정사 → 동시동작 표현에 부적절
det.tip: 분사구문 (동시동작/부대상황): 주절, ~ing ... → 주절과 동시에 일어나는 동작

questions.passage: To study their cooperative behavior, Dr. Hare’s team set up a device __________ required two individuals to pull both ends of a rope at the same time in order to access food on a board. When placed with partners that the chimpanzees knew, they were able to work together to get the food.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 선행사 a device(사물)를 수식하는 주격 관계대명사 which가 적절하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② which: 사물 선행사(a device) + 주격 관계대명사
❌ ① what: 선행사 포함 관계대명사 → 앞에 선행사(a device)가 있으므로 불가
❌ ③ who: 사람 선행사용 → device는 사물
❌ ④ where: 관계부사 → 뒤에 완전한 절이 와야 하나, required의 주어 필요
det.tip: 선행사(사물) + which + 동사: 사물을 수식하는 주격 관계대명사

questions.passage: One possible explanation is that our ancestors lived in larger communities that promoted cooperation and the free exchange of knowledge, while Neanderthals tended to live in smaller groups. These social differences may have given Homo sapiens a competitive advantage over Neanderthals, __________ them to adapt to an ever-changing environment.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 앞 절의 결과를 나타내는 분사구문으로 현재분사 allowing이 적절하다. "이점을 주었고, 그 결과 적응할 수 있게 했다"
det.analysis:
✅ ② allowing: 결과를 나타내는 분사구문 (현재분사)
❌ ① allowed: 과거형 → 접속사 없이 두 절 연결 불가
❌ ③ to allow: to부정사 → 문맥상 결과 표현에 부적절
❌ ④ having allowed: 완료 분사구문 → 주절보다 앞선 동작이 아님
❌ ⑤ allow: 원형 → 문법적으로 불가
det.tip: 결과 분사구문: 주절, ~ing ... → "그 결과 ~하다" (결과를 자연스럽게 이어줌)

questions.passage: When ①<u>placed</u> with partners that the chimpanzees knew, they were able to work together to get the food. However, when ②<u>pairing</u> with new partners, the chimpanzees usually failed to get the food, and when they occasionally ③<u>succeeded</u>, they did not share the food with their partner.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~③ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ② pairing → paired: 침팬지가 짝지어지는 것(수동)이므로 과거분사 paired가 적절하다. "When paired with new partners" = 새로운 짝과 짝지어졌을 때
det.analysis:
❌ ② pairing(능동) → paired(수동): 침팬지가 스스로 짝을 짓는 것이 아니라 실험에서 짝지어진 것
✅ ① placed: 수동 분사구문 → "짝과 함께 놓여졌을 때" 올바름
✅ ③ succeeded: 과거형 동사 → "가끔 성공했을 때" 올바름
det.tip: 분사구문의 능동/수동: 주어가 동작의 주체이면 ~ing(능동), 동작을 당하는 쪽이면 p.p.(수동)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: "He conducted an experiment to see how dogs would respond to human gestures compared to wolves" → Brian Hare가 개와 늑대를 비교하는 실험을 수행했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② Brian Hare가 개와 늑대 대상 실험 수행: 본문과 일치
❌ ① Dr. Wilson은 evolutionary biologist(진화 생물학자)이지 인류학자(anthropologist)가 아님
❌ ③ 늑대는 몸짓에 관심을 보이지 않았음 (개가 더 잘 읽음)
❌ ④ "who share the same common ancestor" → 같은 공통 조상을 공유함
det.tip: 내용 일치: 각 선택지의 핵심 단어를 본문과 정확히 대조

ch: Brian Hare는 개와 늑대를 대상으로 실험을 수행했다.
늑대는 인간의 몸짓을 개보다 더 잘 읽었다.
개와 늑대는 공통된 조상을 가지고 있지 않다.

However, when paired with new partners, the chimpanzees usually failed to get the food, and when they occasionally succeeded, they did not share the food with their partner. The bonobos, on the other hand, got along much better than the chimpanzees. They solved the problem regardless of which individual they were paired with, and they were also more willing to share the food. This research shows that bonobos have a cooperative and friendly nature. Experts suggest that their nature has helped their species survive. Without these characteristics, they could have faced extinction.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.korean: 본문: "the chimpanzees usually failed to get the food, and ... they did not share the food with their partner" → 침팬지는 새 짝과 음식을 나누지 않았다. 따라서 "기꺼이 나누었다"는 본문과 반대.
det.analysis:
❌ ③ 침팬지는 새 짝과 음식을 나누지 않았음 → "did not share"와 반대
✅ ① "genetically similar" → 일치
✅ ② "solved the problem regardless of which individual" → 일치
✅ ④ "Experts suggest that their nature has helped their species survive" → 일치
det.tip: 불일치 문제: 본문 표현과 선택지의 핵심 동사(shared vs. did not share)를 대조

ch: 보노보는 어떤 개체와 짝을 이루든 문제를 해결했다.
침팬지는 새로운 짝과도 음식을 기꺼이 나누었다.
전문가들은 보노보의 본성이 생존에 도움이 되었다고 말한다.

questions.passage: In our competitive society, many people believe that only the biggest or the strongest can survive and thrive. However, I propose an alternative view: kindness is the key to success. Isn’t that a comforting thought? We can use the power of our natural kindness to communicate and cooperate with different individuals. We can all benefit from this instead of trying to be better than others. I’d like to end this talk with a message. Think of our society as a bouquet. Just as each flower adds to the beauty when it harmonizes with the others, each person can contribute to a more beautiful world when they cooperate. By being kind and working together, we can truly flourish. Thank you for your attention.
questions.stem: 이 글(강연) 전체의 목적으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: "kindness is the key to success" + "By being kind and working together, we can truly flourish" → 다정함과 협력이 생존/성공의 핵심이라는 주장
det.analysis:
✅ ③ 다정함과 협력이 생존의 핵심: "kindness is the key to success" + "working together, we can truly flourish"
❌ ① 강한 자만 생존: 오히려 이 견해에 반대하고 있음
❌ ② 네안데르탈인 신체 능력: 본문의 보조 예시일 뿐 주목적 아님
❌ ④ 유전적 차이: 개/늑대는 예시, 목적 아님
❌ ⑤ 보노보 지능: 언급 없음
det.tip: 강연/글의 목적: 결론부에서 핵심 주장이 드러남 → "kindness is the key to success"

ch: 강한 자만이 살아남을 수 있다는 점을 강조하기 위해
네안데르탈인의 뛰어난 신체 능력을 설명하기 위해
다정함과 협력이 생존의 핵심이라고 주장하기 위해
개와 늑대의 유전적 차이를 밝히기 위해
보노보가 침팬지보다 지능이 높다는 것을 증명하기 위해

questions.passage: Dr. Hare concluded that the dogs’ ability to read human gestures allowed them to perform better than the wolves. He explained that dogs, unlike wolves, have developed communicative skills with humans and a sense of friendliness. This explanation sounds reasonable according to several evolutionary biologists. They say that from the common ancestors of these two species, those that acted friendly toward humans evolved into dogs, and those that didn’t became wolves. Furthermore, Dr. Hare suggested that the friendly nature of dogs probably provided them with a __________ that allowed their population to grow larger than that of wolves.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 개의 친근한 본성이 늑대보다 더 많은 개체 수를 증가시킬 수 있게 한 것은 생존의 이점(survival advantage)이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② survival advantage: 친근한 본성 → 인간과의 공존 → 개체 수 증가 = 생존 이점
❌ ① physical strength: 신체적 힘은 언급되지 않음
❌ ③ genetic mutation: 유전자 변이는 본문 맥락과 무관
❌ ④ territorial instinct: 영역 본능은 언급되지 않음
det.tip: 빈칸 뒤의 "allowed their population to grow larger"가 핵심 단서 → 생존에 유리한 이점

questions.passage: Now let’s turn our attention to ourselves, Homo sapiens. How have we managed to survive for so long? Neanderthals existed together with Homo sapiens until about 40,000 years ago, and they were known to be intelligent and physically superior to Homo sapiens. Neanderthals were able to make tools and fire and had strong bodies with well-developed muscles and broad shoulders. Despite these attributes, however, it was Homo sapiens who ultimately survived and thrived. One possible explanation is that our ancestors lived in larger communities that promoted cooperation and the free exchange of knowledge, while Neanderthals tended to live in smaller groups. These social differences may have given Homo sapiens a __________ over Neanderthals, allowing them to adapt to an ever-changing environment.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 호모 사피엔스의 더 큰 공동체와 협력이 네안데르탈인에 비해 경쟁력 있는 이점(competitive advantage)을 제공했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② competitive advantage: 사회적 차이 → 변화하는 환경 적응 = 경쟁적 우위
❌ ① biological similarity: 생물학적 유사성은 이점이 아님
❌ ③ physical barrier: 물리적 장벽은 문맥과 무관
❌ ④ social conflict: 사회적 갈등은 이점이 아님
det.tip: "allowing them to adapt"가 핵심 단서 → 적응을 가능하게 한 이점

questions.passage: A successful presentation relies on employing various presentation skills, such as using friendly gestures, making natural eye contact, and speaking with an appropriate volume. But just as important, well-designed slides play a critical role in effectively __________ your message. Here are some useful tips for improving your presentation slides. First, adopt a "less is more" approach by keeping your slides simple. Limit each slide to five lines of text and use phrases instead of full sentences.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 잘 디자인된 슬라이드는 메시지를 효과적으로 전달하는(conveying) 데 중요한 역할을 한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① conveying(전달하다): 슬라이드의 역할 = 메시지 전달
❌ ② concealing(숨기다): 메시지를 숨기는 것이 아님
❌ ③ complicating(복잡하게 하다): "less is more"와 모순
❌ ④ contradicting(모순되다): 문맥과 반대
det.tip: play a critical role in + ~ing: ~하는 데 중요한 역할을 하다

questions.passage: It’s good to see you, everyone! I’m Dr. Edward Wilson, an evolutionary biologist. Thank you for inviting me here today. On my way, I had trouble locating this room. Luckily, a friendly student came up to me and walked me here. It’s __________ (fascinate) how, in situations like this, we want to help someone in need. Now, this raises some interesting questions: where does our friendliness come from, and why is it important?
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 어법에 맞게 변형하여 쓰시오.

det.korean: fascinate(동사) → fascinating(형용사): "It’s + 형용사" 구문에서 상황이 "흥미로운"이라는 의미의 현재분사형 형용사
det.analysis:
fascinate(동사) → fascinating(형용사)
It’s ______ how ~: "~하는 것은 흥미롭다" → 상황을 설명하는 형용사 필요
-ing형(fascinating): 대상/상황이 흥미를 유발 | -ed형(fascinated): 사람이 흥미를 느끼는
det.tip: It’s + 감정 형용사: 상황/사물 주어 → -ing (fascinating, interesting, surprising)

questions.passage: Dr. Hare concluded that the dogs’ ability to read human gestures allowed them to perform better than the wolves. He explained that dogs, unlike wolves, have developed __________ (communicate) skills with humans and a sense of friendliness. This explanation sounds reasonable according to several evolutionary biologists.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 어법에 맞게 변형하여 쓰시오.

det.korean: communicate(동사) → communicative(형용사): 명사 skills를 수식하는 형용사가 필요. "의사소통의, 소통 능력이 있는"
det.analysis:
communicate(동사) → communicative(형용사)
빈칸 뒤 skills(명사)를 수식하는 형용사가 필요
communicative skills = 의사소통 능력
det.tip: communicate → communicative / create → creative / imagine → imaginative — -ate → -ative 형용사 변환

questions.passage: Dr. Hare concluded that the dogs’ ability to read human gestures allowed them to perform better than the wolves. He explained that dogs, unlike wolves, have developed communicative skills with humans and a sense of friendliness. This explanation sounds reasonable according to several evolutionary biologists. They say that from the common ancestors of these two species, those that acted friendly toward humans evolved into dogs, and those that didn’t became wolves.
questions.stem: 다음 글에서 개가 늑대와 달리 인간과 함께 발달시킨 것 중, 의사소통 능력(communicative skills)과 함께 언급된 것을 본문에서 1단어로 찾아 쓰시오.

det.korean: "dogs have developed communicative skills with humans and a sense of friendliness" → 친밀감 = friendliness
det.analysis:
communicative skills와 and로 연결된 것 = "a sense of friendliness"
1단어 답 = friendliness
det.tip: "본문에서 찾기" 유형: 한글 힌트의 키워드와 대응하는 영어 표현을 정확히 찾기

questions.passage: The bonobos, on the other hand, got along much better than the chimpanzees. They solved the problem regardless of which individual they were paired with, and they were also more willing to share the food. This research shows that bonobos have a cooperative and friendly nature. Experts suggest that their nature has helped their species survive. Without these characteristics, they could have faced extinction.
questions.stem: 다음 글에서 보노보가 협력적이고 친절한 특성이 없었다면 직면했을 수 있었던 것을 본문에서 1단어로 찾아 쓰시오.

det.korean: "Without these characteristics, they could have faced extinction" → 멸종 = extinction
det.analysis:
Without these characteristics → could have faced extinction
협력적 본성이 없었다면 = 멸종에 직면했을 것
det.tip: "could have + p.p." = 가정법 과거완료 → "~했을 수도 있었다" (실제로는 일어나지 않음)

questions.passage: In our competitive society, many people believe that only the biggest or the strongest can survive and thrive. However, I propose an alternative view: kindness is the key to success. Isn’t that a comforting thought? We can use the power of our natural kindness to communicate and cooperate with different individuals. We can all benefit from this instead of trying to be better than others. I’d like to end this talk with a message. Think of our society as a bouquet. Just as each flower adds to the beauty when it harmonizes with the others, each person can contribute to a more beautiful world when they cooperate. By being kind and working together, we can truly flourish. Thank you for your attention.
questions.stem: 다음 글에서 필자가 우리 사회를 비유한 대상을 본문에서 2단어로 찾아 쓰시오.

det.korean: "Think of our society as a bouquet" → 우리 사회를 꽃다발에 비유 = a bouquet
det.analysis:
Think of A as B: A를 B로 생각하다
A = our society, B = a bouquet → 사회를 꽃다발에 비유
det.tip: Think of A as B = A를 B로 비유하다 → 비유 대상을 찾는 문제

questions.passage: It’s good to see you, everyone! I’m Dr. Edward Wilson, an evolutionary biologist. Thank you for inviting me here today. On my way, I had trouble locating this room. Luckily, a friendly student came up to me and walked me here. It’s fascinating how, in situations like this, we want to help someone in need.
questions.stem:
다음 진술이 본문의 내용과 일치하면 True, 일치하지 않으면 False를 고르시오.

"Dr. Wilson had difficulty finding the room on his way to the lecture."

det.korean: "On my way, I had trouble locating this room." → Wilson 박사는 오는 길에 강연실을 찾는 데 어려움을 겪었다. → True
det.analysis: ✅ True: "had trouble locating this room" = "had difficulty finding the room" → 동일한 의미
det.tip: had trouble ~ing = had difficulty ~ing: ~하는 데 어려움을 겪다

questions.passage: The responsive behavior of dogs also caught the attention of an evolutionary anthropologist, Brian Hare. He conducted an experiment to see how dogs would respond to human gestures compared to wolves, who share the same common ancestor. He placed two cups on the ground with food hidden under only one of them. When he pointed to the cup with the food, the dogs found it easily. The wolves, however, struggled and chose cups at random, paying no attention to his gestures.
questions.stem:
다음 진술이 본문의 내용과 일치하면 True, 일치하지 않으면 False를 고르시오.

"The wolves successfully followed Brian Hare’s gestures to find the food."

det.korean: 본문: "The wolves, however, struggled and chose cups at random, paying no attention to his gestures." → 늑대는 몸짓에 관심을 기울이지 않고 무작위로 선택했다. 따라서 "성공적으로 따랐다"는 False.
det.analysis: ❌ False: 본문 "struggled and chose cups at random" → 무작위 선택, 몸짓을 따르지 못함
det.tip: T/F에서 "successfully"와 같은 부사에 주의 → 본문에서 실패/어려움으로 서술된 경우 False

questions.passage: A successful presentation relies on employing various presentation skills, such as using friendly gestures, making natural eye contact, and speaking with an appropriate volume. But just as important, well-designed slides play a critical role in effectively conveying your message. Here are some useful tips for improving your presentation slides. First, adopt a "less is more" approach by keeping your slides simple. Limit each slide to five lines of text and use phrases instead of full sentences. This allows the audience to focus more on listening than on reading. Next, prioritize readability by carefully selecting attractive font sizes and colors. The best readability is generally achieved with a font size of at least 18 pt, and you should limit slides to three or four colors to avoid distraction. Lastly, enhance your slides with high-quality images that complement the text. By following these simple tips, you can create effective slides that hold your audience’s interest and keep them engaged from start to finish!
questions.stem:
다음 진술이 본문의 내용과 일치하면 True, 일치하지 않으면 False를 고르시오.

"You should limit slides to three or four colors to avoid distraction."

det.korean: "you should limit slides to three or four colors to avoid distraction" → 본문과 정확히 일치 → True
det.analysis: ✅ True: 본문 원문 "you should limit slides to three or four colors to avoid distraction"과 진술이 정확히 일치
det.tip: 본문의 문장을 그대로 인용한 진술 → True

questions.passage: Now let’s turn our attention to ourselves, Homo sapiens. How have we managed to survive for so long? Neanderthals existed together with Homo sapiens until about 40,000 years ago, and they were known to be intelligent and physically superior to Homo sapiens. Neanderthals were able to make tools and fire and had strong bodies with well-developed muscles and broad shoulders. Despite these attributes, however, it was Homo sapiens who ultimately survived and thrived. One possible explanation is that our ancestors lived in larger communities that promoted cooperation and the free exchange of knowledge, while Neanderthals tended to live in smaller groups.
questions.stem:
다음 진술이 본문의 내용과 일치하면 True, 일치하지 않으면 False를 고르시오.

"Homo sapiens survived because they were physically stronger than Neanderthals."

det.korean: 본문에서 호모 사피엔스의 생존 이유는 더 큰 공동체에서의 협력과 지식 교환이지, 신체적으로 더 강해서가 아니다. 오히려 네안데르탈인이 "physically superior"했다. → False
det.analysis:
❌ False: 본문 "Neanderthals were known to be physically superior to Homo sapiens" → 네안데르탈인이 신체적으로 우월
호모 사피엔스 생존 이유 = 큰 공동체 + 협력 + 지식 교환
det.tip: 인과 관계를 정확히 파악: 생존 이유 = 신체적 힘(✗) → 사회적 협력과 지식 교환(✓)
